analyst.summary: United Spirits' premiumization story is genuinely working — its premium-and-above portfolio is now nine-tenths of sales and margins keep expanding — but the stock's roughly 55-times trailing-earnings valuation already assumes years of smooth, high-teens profit growth that this business has not actually shown; in the very year it delivered strong numbers, it also absorbed two separate state excise shocks (in Andhra Pradesh and a steep Maharashtra duty hike) that a national spirits company is structurally exposed to almost every year. The Royal Challengers Bengaluru cricket-franchise stake has now been sold for roughly Rs 16,660 crore in cash rather than held as a growth lever, so the current price has to be justified by the core liquor business alone going forward — and on that basis, we think the price is ahead of what the business can reliably deliver. Sell.
